findings: F1-77-l3-security: TAP table, IDCODE/BYPASS rules, SWD packet, EXC_RETURN, xPSR, SysTick, FPB/DWT: unverified box -> confirmed against ADIv5 and the Armv7-M ARM; only the IEEE 1149.1 text itself stays unverified (D3 §B3.2.3, §B3.4, §B4.2; D4)
F1-77-l3-bp: number of breakpoints "in the core TRM" -> Cortex-M3: six instruction comparators (or two), Code region only (D9 §7.1, §7.3)

F1-77-hardware: debug port clocked by the probe "independent of the core clock", usable while core in reset -> DP registers in the always-on power domain, with power-up and reset request bits (D3 §B2.3.1)
F1-77-hardware: comparator match -> debug state "at the next instruction boundary" -> breakpoint halts before the instruction; watchpoint is asynchronous, halts after the access (D4 C1.8.1, C1.11.1)
F1-77-l2-jtag: "small packages often offer only SWD" -> SWJ-DP switches between SWD and JTAG; RP2350 is SWD-only (D3 §B5.2; D13 §1.2.2)
F1-77-breaks: debugger reads of a UART receive register clear flags (Yiu) -> RP2350 FIFO reads remove data; SysTick COUNTFLAG is not cleared by debugger reads (D13 App. A; D4 B3.3.3)
F1-77-l3-bp: QEMU breakpoints "inside the emulator" (no source) -> QEMU advertises an infinite number of hardware breakpoints and watchpoints for TCG (D6 §GDB usage)
unverified: F1-77-l3-security: IEEE Std 1149.1 text not opened (sold); TAP rules taken from Arm's JTAG-DP
